title: Proposal for Enclosed HDB Deck Space to be Designated Pedestrian-only Paths to Prevent Accidents with PMDs
what_it_is: Proposal for Enclosed HDB Deck Space to be Designated Pedestrian-only Paths to Prevent Accidents with PMDs

sections.label: Void deck PMD pedestrian-only paths
sections.summary: Asked whether enclosed void deck space may be designated pedestrian-only paths under the Active Mobility Act, and Town Councils can set and enforce their own PMD rules there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Transport whether enclosed void deck space in HDB housing estates covering the ground floor lift lobbies and letter box areas may be designated as pedestrian-only paths under the Active Mobility Act to reduce the risk of collision between PMD users and block residents in these areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Thus, Town Councils can set and enforce their own rules on the usage of personal mobility devices (PMDs) in such areas, including banning their use.

sections.label: Void decks exempted from Act
sections.summary: Void decks have been exempted from the Active Mobility Act because of multiple blind spots from pillars and because they are not critical for connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: Bearing in mind these three key considerations, void decks have been exempted from the Active Mobility Act because they have, first of all, multiple blind spots due to the presence of pillars and they are not critical for connectivity since cyclists and PMD users can dismount and push for the last leg of their journey at the void decks.

sections.label: Void deck definition and PMD bans
sections.summary: Letter box areas, ground floor lift lobbies and corridors fronting residential flats are considered void decks, so Town Councils can impose a ban on PMD use there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: In the definition of void decks, letter box areas and ground floor lift lobbies, as well as corridors fronting residential flats, are considered as void decks.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: As such, Town Councils can exercise the flexibility of imposing a ban on PMD use in those areas.

sections.label: Town Council officers as wardens
sections.summary: The Act does not allow Town Council employees to be appointed public path wardens, and discussions are ongoing on amending the law.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The current Active Mobility Act actually does not allow Town Council employees to be appointed as public path wardens to enforce the Active Mobility Act in the areas that Er Dr Lee Bee Wah had mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: We have taken that into consideration and we are currently discussing with the Land Transport Authority and the Attorney-General's Chamber to see if the law can be amended to allow for Town Council officers to enforce active mobility offences in such areas.

sections.label: Banning PMDs under by-laws
sections.summary: If a Town Council feels banning PMD use at void decks is necessary, it can be done under the Town Council by-laws.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: If the Town Council feels that the banning of PMD use at void decks is necessary, it can be done under the Town Council by-laws.
